# Cortex plan-first retrieval log

**Status:** [WIP] — companion log for `plans/cortex-plan-first-retrieval.plans.md` (same workstream boundary; created per the tracker-handoff convention). Completed-step packets and compressed evidence summaries are archived here; the tracker keeps a compact [DONE] marker plus a reference to this file. This file is not gate-parsed — the tracker's fenced YAML packets remain the machine contract.

**Archived on:** the A8 compression pass (PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A8, the USER directive "Tidy Cortex tracker: all Phase1 steps/slices done; archive completed evidence to companion .logs.md with recoverable packets, compact plan, mark Phase2 active"). **Archived content:** the Phase-1 phase packet, the Step-01 / Step-02 / Step-03 packets, the whole `## Latest validation evidence` body, the nine `fix_packet` blocks and the thirteen historical `## Handoff query` paragraphs — all BYTE-EXACT, with the SHA-256 of each archived region recorded below.

**Archived on (the A9 batch):** the PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A9 compaction (the USER directive, verbatim: "Finalize Cortex plan: Phase2 all green; archive completed packets/evidence into existing .logs.md, compact active tracker, preserve pending racer handoff and unresolved RAG gaps; mark workstream done; gates/plan-sync."). **Archived content:** FIVE MORE REGIONS, ALL BYTE-EXACT AND SHA-256 VERIFIED - the measured-baseline `## Current state`, the `red_evidence` of `P1-S2-1`, the `implementation_evidence` of `P1-S2-3`, the full PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A8 and the superseded `## Handoff query` - under `## Evidence archive - Phase 2 (byte-exact) - the PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A9 compaction`. **THE "Phase2 all green" PREMISE WAS MEASURED FALSE AND WAS REFUSED; THE WORKSTREAM WAS NOT CLOSED.** THE A9 BATCH CLOSE IS THE LAST SECTION OF THIS FILE.

**THE ARCHIVE IS A MOVE, NOT A COPY.** The tracker no longer carries the verbose Phase-1 history; the bytes live here. The corpus contract ALREADY preserves every `.logs.md` tracker inside the `plan` family (`plans/**/*.md` minus `plans/completed/**`), so this file adds NO new log family and NO new tracker boundary.

THEY KEEP THEIR DETERMINISTIC IDs AND THEIR HTML ANCHOR COMMENTS, SO A CORTEX RAG QUERY RESOLVES THEM DIRECTLY.

**THE ROUTING RULE FOR A NEW FIX LOOP.** When the orchestrator dispatches a NEW `04-implementing` instance for a fix packet, the prompt contains ONLY the deterministic id and the RAG load instruction: `Execute fix-packet-<slice_id>-iteration-<n>. Load context via Cortex MCP / search_context with query 'fix-packet-<slice_id>-iteration-<n>'.` The archived block below is what that query resolves.

**`P1-S2-3` HAS NO FIX PACKET - DELIBERATELY** (APPROVE on iteration 1, no repair cycle needed). `P1-S1-5` HAS NO iteration-4 PACKET (its fourth round passed on the canonical `fix-loop` marker alone).

## The archive and its integrity

Each archived region below was moved OUT of the tracker BYTE-EXACT. The SHA-256 is computed over the UTF-8 bytes of the region text with CRLF line terminators, and it is the same value before the move (read from the pre-A8 tracker) and after the move (re-read from THIS file) — the tracker is UNTRACKED in git (`V-OBS-029`), so there is NO git safety net and these checksums ARE the preservation evidence.

## Phase 1 — archived phase and step packets (byte-exact)

Archived verbatim from the tracker at the Phase-1 -> `[DONE]` flip (PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A8). The archived packets carry the HISTORICAL step numbering and the HISTORICAL statuses (`Step 02` is `[PLANNED]` here because that was its state when it was archived); PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A8 in the tracker records the move of `Step 02` to Phase 2 as `Step 07`.

### Phase 1 — The corpus contract: deterministic families, no generated noise, bounded memory [WIP]

**Phase objective:** ONE published corpus-family contract, the target family set (the `readme` and `benchmark` families retired, the `test` family added, the generated READMEs and the session snapshot excluded), and the bounded-memory proof for the `rag:update` pipeline.

**Phase progression rule:** Phase 1 stays [WIP] until the corpus-family contract, the parity wave and the bounded-memory `rag:update` proof are ALL closed. The phase NEVER advances to [DONE] on a partial corpus, and Step 02 / Step 03 NEVER start before Step 01 closes its acceptance criteria.

RESTATED BY PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A5 - the peak-RSS comparison is ONE bound: the post-change peak RSS is the MEDIAN of N >= 5 runs of the SAME probe against the POST-change corpus, and that MEDIAN MUST NOT exceed the ORIGINALLY FROZEN ceiling of 585,711,616 bytes; there is NO allowance of any kind (the A4 percentage allowance is DELETED), and the re-frozen multi-sample pre-change median is the NOISE REFERENCE for the measurement protocol, NOT a second threshold.'
  - 'AC-204: no stale family survives anywhere - the entity-type map, the per-family freshness rules, the eval fixtures, the eval runner, the family table in `rag-index/README.md`, the FOUR family-pinning test homes (the entity-graph family-count home `rag-index/build-entity-graph.test.mjs` is owned by the Step-1 GREEN slice `P1-S1-4`; the other three are owned by the Step-2 parity wave) and the index rows themselves are all re-pointed at the surviving families IN THE SAME STEP that removes the retired families (no deferred cleanup).'

## Evidence archive — Phase 1 (byte-exact)

Archived verbatim from the tracker at the A8 compression pass: the WHOLE `## Latest validation evidence` body — the authoring evidence, the six VERIFICATION VERDICTs, the PLAN AMENDMENT RECORDS A1-A7, every per-slice evidence block, every measurement transcript, the sixteen canonical `fix-loop:` markers and every `V-OBS-###` entry.

**Authoring evidence (this pass wrote plan bytes ONLY - no production, test, spec, index or bundle byte was touched):**

**1. THE THREE OWNED FILES AND WHAT EACH ONE DOES NOW.**

| file                          | what changed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rag-index/ts-chunker.mjs`    | the module-scope `import { Node, Project } from 'ts-morph'` is GONE; a CACHED LAZY LOADER (`node:module` `createRequire` + `requireTsMorph` + `loadTsMorphModule()`) loads ts-morph on first use; the new exported `getTsMorphNode()` hands the `Node` class to the call sites that need it; `createTypeScriptProject` keeps its SYNCHRONOUS signature and options; the new exported `releaseTypeScriptProject(project)` releases the AST through the REAL ts-morph surfaces only - `project.removeSourceFile(sourceFile)` for every source file, then `project.getLanguageService().compilerObject.dispose()` - because the Project has NO `dispose()` and NO `forget()` and NEITHER is called; it is null-guarded, `WeakSet`-idempotent, and the live-node holders are nulled BEFORE the release. |
| `rag-index/ts-chunker-v2.mjs` | the module-scope `import { Node } from 'ts-morph'` is GONE; the per-file body was factored into a private `chunkFileDeclarations(filePath, fileDeclarations)` that BOTH the flat API and the new streaming API call, so the two paths cannot drift; the new exported `async function* chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2Stream(options)` yields the per-document chunk groups; it returns BEFORE creating a Project when there are no source paths, and it releases ONLY a project it created ITSELF (a caller-supplied `options.project` is never released here - the ownership contract of `loadExportedTypeScriptDeclarations` is unchanged).                                                                                                                                                              |
| `rag-index/build-index.mjs`   | the whole-build `tsSourceChunksByFilePath` Map and its `collectTypeScriptChunksByFilePath` collector are DELETED; the named import became a NAMESPACE import (`import * as tsChunkerV2`) so the frozen test host's mock (which provides ONLY `chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2`) still links; a new private `createTypeScriptChunkSource(tsSourcePaths)` exposes `{ take(filePath), close() }`; `take()` is fed by a LAZY ASYNC ITERATOR over the stream with a bounded buffer of not-yet-matching groups; the source is CLOSED at the ts-source family boundary (and once in the `finally`), where the best-effort `forceHeapRelease()` runs.                                                                                                                                                              |

**2. `AC-203-G-IMPL-A` - THE AST IS RELEASED AND THE IMPORT IS LAZY (SATISFIED).** Neither chunker holds a module-scope ts-morph binding any more, and ts-morph is loaded on the chunking path only. The AST is released through the surfaces that actually exist in ts-morph 27.0.2 / TypeScript 5.x - `Project.removeSourceFile()` (which forgets the node) followed by `project.getLanguageService().compilerObject.dispose()` - and NOT through the non-existent `Project.dispose()` / `Project.forget()`. The equivalence is RECORDED in item 5 and the before/after resident-set figures are RECORDED in item 6. The empirical confirmation that the compiler is no longer resident at chunk time is the PRE-CHUNKING resident set: **104,728 KB BEFORE -> 61,212 KB AFTER** (and 60,888 KB on an independent re-run), i.e. the ts-morph compiler is simply NOT LOADED until the ts-source family is chunked.

**3. `AC-203-G-IMPL-B` - PER-DOCUMENT CHUNKING, THE WHOLE-BUILD MAP IS NOT MATERIALISED (SATISFIED).** The resident ts-chunk set went from O(corpus) to O(one document): `build-index.mjs` no longer holds a Map of all 21,013 ts-source chunk records; it pulls one document's group at a time through `take(filePath)` and closes the source at the family boundary. The corpus census and the chunk count were captured BEFORE and AFTER and THEY AGREE - **9 families, 1,848 documents, 21,013 chunks** on both sides, with the same per-family document counts (`ts-source` 516, `demo` 664, `test` 339, `completed-plan` 211, `skill` 67, `agent` 39, `plan` 8, `root-doc` 3, `copilot-instructions` 1) and the same per-document chunk ORDER (proved by the digests in item 5, not by inspection). The stream reuses the GLOBAL declaration de-dup and the SAME visiting order, which is what makes byte-identity possible at all: `loadExportedTypeScriptDeclarations` de-dups on `${declarationFile}:${declaration.getStart()}:${declaration.getKindName()}` keeping the FIRST-VISITED entry, and the survivor decides whether a symbol becomes a substantive chunk or a module-index stub - a per-file independent de-dup would NOT be byte-identical.

**4. `AC-203-G-IMPL-C` - THE FROZEN FIXTURE, THE RED HOME AND THE CEILING ARE UNTOUCHED (SATISFIED).** `rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-baseline.json` was NOT edited, NOT regenerated and NOT re-pinned; the ceiling stays **585,711,616 B** and the replica figure stays **111,783,936 B**; `rag-index/__tests__/corpus-contract.red.test.mjs` was NOT edited; NO production file outside the three was edited; NO second threshold, NO tolerance and NO margin was introduced anywhere; the measured post-remediation datum is RECORDED in item 6 and HANDED to the GREEN lane `P1-S3-3` in item 13; and **THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM THE BOUND IS MET.**

**THE GOVERNING RULE (ONE rule, stated once, used in EVERY governing clause).**

1. **THE MEASUREMENT** - the post-change peak RSS is the **MEDIAN of N >= 5 runs** of the **SAME probe** against the **POST-change corpus**. The per-run peak and the run spread are RECORDED beside the median, but the per-run peak is NOT the measured quantity that the bound is applied to.
2. **THE BOUND** - that MEDIAN **MUST NOT exceed 585,711,616 bytes**, the ORIGINALLY FROZEN ceiling recorded in `rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-baseline.json`. The comparison is `median <= 585711616`, exactly.
3. **NO ALLOWANCE OF ANY KIND** - no percentage, no tolerance band, no margin, no rounding slack above that ceiling. **NO clause of this plan grants a bound above 585,711,616 bytes.** The A4 percentage-allowance wording is **DELETED**, not merely superseded, and NO surviving clause carries a second reading.
4. **THE PRE-CHANGE ARM IS A PROTOCOL OBLIGATION, NOT A THRESHOLD** - the pre-change baseline is still RE-FROZEN as a multi-sample median (run count, median, minimum, maximum, spread) captured by the SAME probe and recorded in the frozen fixture, which KEEPS every key the RED home asserts, **MAY ONLY ADD** those statistics and is **NEVER silently regenerated** (re-baselining after seeing the result would be circular). The re-frozen multi-sample median is the **NOISE REFERENCE** for the measurement protocol; it is **NOT a second threshold** and **NOT an allowance**.
5. **WHY A MEDIAN AND NOT AN ALLOWANCE** - the single-sample strict comparison is UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN on a process-lifetime high-water mark whose measured same-corpus spread is 6.45 % (37,363,712 bytes between two runs 51 ms apart, `V-OBS-009`). The MEDIAN of N >= 5 is the CORRECTION to the SAMPLING, not a relaxation of the BOUND. The measured spread stays recorded as a measurement; it is NEVER a tolerance.
6. **THE OTHER THREE NUMBERS ARE UNCHANGED AND STAY EXACT HARD GATES** - replica <= 111,783,936 bytes; documents == 1,848 == 2,080 - 173 - 58 - 1; chunks <= 33,008.

### `P1-S3-3` GREEN EVIDENCE (the INDEPENDENT re-measurement of the A5 bounded-memory arm after the `P1-S3-4` remediation - the memory arm is MET; the full `rag:update` chain is NOT GREEN)

**Author and scope.** `05-green-testing` (Tier 1, the `P1-S3-3` GREEN lane) -> `slice-validator` (Tier 3, read-only slice compliance) -> `coverage-analyst` (Tier 3, read-only coverage measurement). **THE BOUND IS CLAIMED ONLY WHERE IT WAS MEASURED.** This lane EDITED exactly ONE repository file: `rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-baseline.json`, ADDITIVELY, inside its own new `multiSample.postRemediation` key; it APPENDED to this plan; it wrote measurement artifacts ONLY inside the gitignored `tmp/` path. NO production byte was edited. NO test, spec, index or bundle byte was edited. NO git mutation command (`add` / `commit` / `push` / `checkout` / `reset` / `stash`) was run - read-only git inspection only.

**0. THE ONE-LINE VERDICT.** `AC-203-GREEN` **MET** - the post-remediation MEDIAN of N = 5 is **563,331,072 bytes** against the UNCHANGED frozen ceiling of **585,711,616 bytes**, i.e. **22,380,544 bytes (3.821 %) OF HEADROOM**, with NO allowance of any kind, and the other three hard gates are met EXACTLY. `AC-203-D-GREEN` **NOT MET**, and NOT SATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, for TWO independent reasons: the RED home it names DOES NOT EXIST on disk, and the full `npm run rag:update` chain ABORTS DETERMINISTICALLY at the `build-graph` stage with exit 134 (a V8 heap OOM). `AC-206-B` **NOT MET** - the `validate` stage never ran, and its per-stage peak-memory clause is UNMEASURABLE because the per-stage peak publication (`AC-203-C`, owned by `P1-S3-2`) was never implemented. **THE SLICE IS NOT `[DONE]`. `04-implementing` was NOT dispatched by this lane.**

**1. THE MEMORY ARM - `AC-203-GREEN` IS MET (the re-measurement the `P1-S3-4` lane handed over).** THE PROTOCOL (the A5 protocol, not a new one): ONE run per node process, because `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is a PROCESS-LIFETIME high-water mark; EVERY sample enters the median (no warm-up discard, no outlier exclusion, no trimming); TWO arms over TWO instruments - the PRIMARY arm is the plan-mandated control `tmp/p1-s1-4-control.mjs --arm=post` (reads `process.resourceUsage()` BEFORE `readIndexCensus()`, i.e. the LOWER reading) and the CORROBORATING arm is the UNMODIFIED repository probe `rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-probe.mjs` (reads it AFTER the census, i.e. the HIGHER, more CONSERVATIVE reading - and the instrument that produced the frozen ceiling). The corroborating arm was invoked with `--out=tmp/...` on EVERY run, because the probe's DEFAULT `--out` OVERWRITES the frozen fixture. The load conditions were quiet, each sample ran in its own process, and 17,764 MB of physical memory was free before the arm started.

BYTE IDENTITY - THE REMEDIATION'S OWN SURFACE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL.** The `P1-S3-4` lane handed over the claim that the ts-source chunk output is unchanged; this lane re-measured it INDEPENDENTLY with two instruments. `tmp/p1-s3-4-chunk-snapshot.mjs` over the 516 ts-source documents / 2,616 chunks / 438 files gives `corpusSha256 = 35251d11c8a43275291f257c74a2217662b9295c8db842ffbf0796245ef1a64d` - an **EXACT match** with the `P1-S3-4` value. `tmp/p1-s3-4-db-digest.mjs` over a full temporary-database build (9 families / 1,848 documents / 21,030 chunks) gives `corpusIdentity = 841a8a69b63d6aa7d6e9ea1624860c8199dfddf7c549e6537c7fd2f33752d597` - an **EXACT match** with the `P1-S3-4` value. **THE FULL-CORPUS DIGESTS DIFFER, AND THE DELTA IS FULLY ATTRIBUTED:** `documentDigest = 5bc7d28ffd007ec13a3117fbacd0e6cf9b455e929336d7de96a01a5f7d3812a8` (the `P1-S3-4` value was `78c67c2a35395dcd4b8da703dc3bb6e83b842c4979e10778ce51a651c29863fd`) and `chunkDigest = a9bd3c8d351bbe22790b629210cc76ee9a582a8247d58edf18186e706713b4c6` (the `P1-S3-4` value was `6efb8639b2a8bfde3263e13532775dbe514318ecb514797c5ed99d7f6abe6f34`). THE TWO OOM SUITES ARE **HEAP-CAP-BOUND, NOT LOGIC-BOUND**: at the ambient 8,192 MB cap they crash with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`, and at a 12,288 MB cap **both suites pass, 2 suites / 9 tests green**. **4. THE FULL `npm run rag:update` CHAIN - `AC-203-D-GREEN` AND `AC-206-B` ARE NOT MET. THE ROOT CAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESISED.** The chain was run TWICE and **FAILED IDENTICALLY BOTH TIMES** (deterministic, not a flake): `build: ok (1234ms)`, `prewarm-embed: ok (5596ms)`, `build-terms: ok (99384ms)`, **`build-graph: failed (24351ms)`** with **exit status 134** and `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` at 8191.7 MB; `snapshot` and `validate` were **cancelled** because the chain aborts. The failure is **HEAP-CAP-BOUND, NOT LOGIC-BOUND**: the SAME stage run as `node --max-old-space-size=12288 rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs --dry-run --json` **exits 0** in 25,644 ms and reports 10,277 entities / 25,957 edges (code 3,693 / 20,259, doc 6,584 / 5,595, cross-ref 103), with a measured **peak working set of 11,324,051,456 bytes (10.80 GiB)** against the ambient 8 GiB cap. **THE ROOT CAUSE IS A PRE-EXISTING RETENTION DEFECT IN `rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs:373-396` (`buildHeadingTextMap`):** for EVERY doc entity it re-reads the ENTIRE source file with `readFile(absolutePath, 'utf8')` and then retains `content.slice(char_start, char_end)` in `headingsByDoc`. **EACH RETAINED SLICE IS A V8 SlicedString THAT PINS ITS ENTIRE PARENT**, so a 9.3 MB parent is pinned once per entity. THE ACCOUNTING IS MEASURED: **6,584 file reads totalling 5,239,687,219 bytes read from disk out of only 25,845,342 bytes of actual file content - a 203x READ AMPLIFICATION** - dominated by `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md` (9,311,682 bytes, 525 entities, about 4.89 GB of redundant reads). THE DEFECT IS **BYTE-IDENTICAL TO HEAD** (the only diff in that file is the `P1-S1-3` `DOC_ENTITY_SOURCES` -> `CORPUS_SOURCES` swap), and `collectDocDocuments()` (line 347) is filesystem-derived and NOT freshness-gated.

**5. THE `P1-S1-3` CORPUS-CONTRACT CHANGE IS EXONERATED BY AN A/B MEASUREMENT.** A published-contract versus legacy-list A/B over the same corpus measured **6,584** doc entities under the PUBLISHED 9-family contract against **11,734** under the HEAD 7-family list (1,388 documents) - the published contract produces **STRICTLY LESS** pressure, not more. The remediation `P1-S3-4` is exonerated by the same evidence: its `rag-index/ts-chunker.mjs` diff is a lazy CJS ts-morph loader plus a new `releaseTypeScriptProject(project)` that the entity graph never calls, and phase 1 - the only phase that touches the ts-chunker - completes cleanly at a 488 MB peak.

**6. The deviation is recorded in the RED home header AND in the slice packet. **OWNER: the next plan act** - either `AC-206-A` is narrowed to the validator seam, or a slice is given the obligation.
- **`V-OBS-045` (NEW) - the PER-STAGE PEAK FIELD NAME IS NOT PINNED BY THE PLAN.** `AC-203-B` requires a per-stage PEAK MEMORY figure and `AC-203-C` requires the runner to OBTAIN the child stage peak "through a measurement THE RUNNER OWNS", but no clause names the field the stage report carries it under - and a RED home that hard-codes a guessed name is RED FOR THE WRONG REASON. **THE RED LANE THEREFORE TOLERATES A DOCUMENTED CANDIDATE SET**: the injected runner double publishes the figure under EVERY alias (`peakMemoryBytes`, `peakRssBytes`, `peakBytes`, `peakMemory`, `maxRssBytes`, `maxRSS`) AND answers any other peak-like property read off the runner result through a `Proxy` fallback, the child's stdout carries the same aliases as ONE pure-JSON line, and the detector accepts a positive finite number under any key matching `/peak|rss|memory|resident|highwater|hwm/i`. **RECOMMENDED SPELLING FOR `P1-S3-2`: `peakMemoryBytes`** (the plan does not require it; the lane satisfies any spelling). The IDENTITY function name, by contrast, IS pinned by the plan (`AC-203-E` names `computeCorpusIdentity`), so the lane reads exactly that name - off the module namespace through a DYNAMIC `await import`, NEVER a static named import, so the V-BLK-001 defect class is not repeated.

The second declared command `npm run rag:update` WAS ALSO RUN - TWICE: the first run failed at the `build-terms` stage with `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked` (a transient lock against a concurrent writer, NOT a defect of this slice), and the second run reached `build-graph`, which aborted with exit code 134 (a V8 heap OOM at the ambient 8192 MB cap - owned by `P1-S3-5`), so `snapshot` and `validate` were CANCELLED. Because the chain never reached the hash write, the one-time corpus-hash invalidation recorded above is STILL NOT CONSUMED and `rag-index/data/corpus-hash.json` is BYTE-UNCHANGED.

**THE STATUS IS RESTORED TO `[DONE]`.** The round-2 verdict is APPROVE with NO blockers, so the slice status is flipped back from `[WIP]` to `[DONE]`. The three round-1 HIGH blockers (F1, F2, F3) are DISCHARGED.

**THE DECLINED OPTIONALS, WITH THE CORRECT RATIONALE (recorded, not absorbed).** `F4` (an approximate, last-marker-wins sampler) is DECLINED: an approximate figure published under a peak-like key would be picked up by the READ-ONLY RED detector, whose `toPositiveFiniteNumber` accepts any positive finite number under a key matching `/peak|rss|memory|resident|highwater|hwm/i` - so an approximate figure could be read as the EXACT stage figure and break the RED contract that cannot be edited. The obligation that `F4` would have served (a MEASURED peak working set for the `build-graph` stage that aborts with exit 134) is already ROUTED to `P1-S3-5` by `F3`, and `P1-S3-5` owns the `build-graph` stage itself, so it can own the sampler. `F5` (a single-pass identity composition) is DECLINED: the SQL `ORDER BY file_path` uses the SQLite BINARY collation while the exported pure function sorts by JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit order, so letting the internal path skip the sort could make the two paths DISAGREE on a non-ASCII path - a determinism regression that outweighs a 3.74 ms saving. The exported function therefore KEEPS its order-independence, which is what lets `AC-203-E` be pinned without touching the live index.

**THE STORED-DIGEST WORDING IS CORRECTED (the round-1 `F6` INFO finding).** The `P1-S3-2` implementation evidence above says the stored `rag-index/data/corpus-hash.json` "still carries the old 4-field digest `f74ba11b...`". That wording is STALE: the stored digest `f74ba11b...` matches NEITHER the live four-field digest (`44b9e12b...`) NOR the live five-field digest (`1c706dec...`), because the corpus MOVED after that digest was written (the `build` stage re-indexed documents during the declared `npm run rag:update` run of this lane, and other lanes moved the corpus too). The CORRECT statement is: the stored digest is STALE with respect to the live corpus under EITHER identity shape, so the first `npm run rag:update` after this change re-runs `build-graph` instead of skipping it - which is the EXPECTED one-time invalidation `AC-203-E` asks to be RECORDED, and it is NOT yet consumed, because the `build-graph` stage aborts with exit 134 (owned by `P1-S3-5`) and the runner therefore never rewrites the hash file. The stored hash file was VERIFIED unchanged by this lane (`rag-index/data/corpus-hash.json`, mtime 2026-11-16 02:17:46, digest `f74ba11b...`).

**THE FORWARD READING RULE FOR THE GREEN LANE (`C4`, recorded so it is not absorbed silently).** A stage spawned in `--dry-run` mode is a REAL child process, so it publishes a REAL peak figure; ONLY its `status` (`dry-run` rather than `ok`) separates that figure from a full-run figure. A consumer of the stage reports - the `P1-S3-3` GREEN lane and the `AC-206-B` clause in particular - MUST compare FULL-RUN figures only (stages with `status: 'ok'`), otherwise the memory arm can be satisfied VACUOUSLY by a dry-run figure.

**1. THE DEFECT AND THE REPAIR (the OLD path is DELETED, there is NO dual path and NO shim).** BEFORE, `buildHeadingTextMap` (`rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs:373-396` in the HEAD bytes) called `readFile` on the WHOLE FILE once per DOCUMENT ENTITY and kept `content.slice(char_start, char_end)` for every heading it retained; a V8 `SlicedString` pins its ENTIRE parent buffer, so the resident set scaled with (entities x file size) instead of with (the text actually kept). AFTER, the function is a THREE-PHASE pipeline: (1) `groupDocEntitiesByFile` groups the doc entities by `file_path`, the map's insertion order following the FIRST APPEARANCE of each path and each group keeping the original entity order; (2) `readFileSafely` reads each DISTINCT FILE EXACTLY ONCE and `materializeSectionText` copies each retained section into an independent FLAT string (never a `SlicedString`), so the file buffer becomes reclaimable as soon as the read loop ends; (3) the parent -> section arrays are assembled in the ORIGINAL entity order, so the per-parent section ORDER is unchanged. The per-entity re-read was DELETED, not bypassed.

**2. THE READ COUNTS - BOTH BASES ARE RECORDED, AND THE BASIS IS NAMED IN THE CODE.** The published counters are now SCOPE-TRUE (`docHeadingMapFileReadCount`, `docHeadingMapFileBytesRead`, `docHeadingMapDistinctFileCount`, `headingTextBytes`) and BOTH `@returns` blocks state that they measure THE HEADING-TEXT PATH ONLY and are NOT stage-wide read counts - the FP-1 correction of the round-1 review.

### `P1-S3-5` SPECIALIST REVIEW EVIDENCE - ROUND 2 (the re-review of the fix round; severity FULL; the verdict APPROVE and the CLOSED fix loop)

**The chain.** The severity gate (`--json --input=rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs`) reported **severity FULL / specialistCount 1** for the SECOND time, so the Tier-2 `review-coordinator` dispatched EXACTLY ONE **FRESH** Tier-3 `performance-reviewer` - no second reviewer, no re-use of the round-1 instance, no self-review. The verdict was **APPROVE** with **ZERO blockers** and an EMPTY requested-changes list.

**What the round-2 reviewer independently confirmed.** (1) **FP-1 IS DISCHARGED** - the published counters are `docHeadingMapFileReadCount` / `docHeadingMapFileBytesRead` / `docHeadingMapDistinctFileCount`, and BOTH `@returns` blocks (the module-level one and the `buildHeadingTextMap` one) now state that they measure the HEADING-TEXT PATH ONLY and are NOT stage-wide counts; the reviewer confirmed that ZERO stale old counter names remain in production code. (2) **FP-2 IS DISCHARGED** - `headingTextBytes` accumulates `Buffer.byteLength(sectionText, UTF8_ENCODING)` (a true byte count) and the JSDoc states the differing bases (a RETAINED-TEXT byte count against a BYTES-READ-FROM-DISK count) and that the two must not be compared. (3) **FP-3 IS DISCHARGED** - `materializeSectionText` detects EXACTLY the two possible edge-damage modes (a FIRST code unit that is a lone low surrogate, a LAST code unit that is a lone high surrogate) and takes the UTF-16LE round trip, which preserves lone surrogates EXACTLY and still yields a FLAT (non-`SlicedString`) copy, so the "no retained parent buffer" property holds in BOTH branches; the reviewer confirmed that the ONLY `readFile` site is the single per-distinct-file read and the ONLY `slice` site is immediately copied flat. (4) **OUTPUT INVARIANCE** - the OLD-vs-NEW digests are identical (heading map, cross-ref edges, entities) and the live stage still publishes 10,277 entities / 25,957 edges, matching the 12 GB reference run. (5) **AMBIENT-HEAP COMPLETION** - the dry-run exits 0 at 17,490 ms with a 619,675,648 B peak, the full `npm run rag:update` exits 0 with the runner-published `build-graph.peakMemoryBytes` of 895,569,920 B and NO `peakMeasurementUnavailable` marker, and the two owned proof homes are 6/6 + 3/3 PASS at the 8,192 MB ambient cap.

**The seven non-blocking observations carried forward.** **R-1** - `AC-203-GRAPH-A` is worded at STAGE scope ("reads MUST be at most the number of distinct files") while the stage performs 1,978 reads over 989 paths (EXACTLY 2 per path, the second read being `rag-index/extract-doc-entities.mjs:56`, OUTSIDE this slice's boundary); the heading-text path meets the bound exactly, so closing the LITERAL wording needs a plan amendment or a NEW owner, not an in-slice edit. **R-2** - the slice-scoped shared-validation artifact covers the sibling unit home + build + lint only, so the two PROOF homes and `rag:update` exist only in the plan evidence block and MUST be re-measured by the GREEN lane. **R-3** (LOW) - a redundant `Buffer.byteLength` re-scan of ~26.7 MB per run where `buf.length` would be free. **R-4** (LOW) - in the UTF-16LE branch a lone surrogate is counted as 3 bytes against 2 retained (0 of 6,584 sections affected today). **R-5** (LOW, NON-OWNED) - a stale comment at `rag-index/build-entity-graph.test.mjs:702` ("readFile called for each doc entity"); the assertion passes only because the 5 fixture entities use 5 distinct files. **R-6 / R-7** (LOW, NON-OWNED, already routed as FP-6 / FP-5) - `rag-index/extract-cross-refs.mjs:87` joins the flat sections to full length before truncating to 2,000 chars (a transient ~26.7 MB copy), and `rag-index/extract-doc-entities.mjs:91` still pins ~36.2 MB.

**THE FIX LOOP FOR THIS SLICE IS CLOSED.** The round-1 `status=failed` marker is NOT retracted; the canonical history is `iteration 1 status=failed`, `iteration 2 status=passed`. NO production byte and NO test byte was written by this iteration - the iteration-2 CODE delta was written by the FRESH `implementation-executor` instance and is recorded in the `P1-S3-5` IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE block.

The broaden-on-empty fallback (`scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-corpus.mjs:927-940`) then silently re-runs the search with NO family filter and reports `family_fallback: true` / `classification_fallback: true`. A live `search_corpus` call for a plan-shaped query returned a `skill`-family chunk. The plan families are therefore NOT enforced today, and the failure is silent.

**The module-scope TypeScript parse in the published corpus contract (measured).** `rag-index/corpus-sources.mjs` loads and parses `scripts/generate-docs/generate-docs.constants.ts` AT MODULE SCOPE through a `node:module` `createRequire` bridge (the loader near `:48`, the bridge at `:52`, the eager `const DOCS_TARGETS = loadDocsTargets();` at `:78`), so EVERY importer of the corpus contract pays a TypeScript parse on import - even the consumers that only need the target roots. The measured cost of that import is **+27,252 KB (+26.6 MB)** of resident memory over a plain ESM control module and **+28,252 KB (+27.6 MB)** over bare `node`, with `heapUsed` rising from 4.40 MB to 12.64 MB, and the P1-S1-4 probe recorded it as `module_load_cost_bytes: 27,913,280`. The parse CANNOT be made lazy: the published `DOCS_TARGET_ROOTS` and the `GENERATED_README_IGNORE` list are DERIVED from the parsed constants (`rag-index/corpus-sources.mjs:137`), so the contract can only become cheap if the docs-generator target roots are published AS PLAIN DATA and the link back to the generator is held by a GUARD TEST instead of by the production module. That is what slice `P1-S1-5` does (ONE file, `rag-index/corpus-sources.mjs`), and the guard test is owned by `P1-S2-1` under `AC-202-B`.

**The residual bounded-memory defect (the never-released ts-morph AST and the whole-build ts-chunk Map).** The module-scope TypeScript parse of `rag-index/corpus-sources.mjs` was the FIRST half of the resident-memory regression; the SECOND half is still in the code. `rag-index/ts-chunker.mjs:18` imports ts-morph at MODULE SCOPE, `createTypeScriptProject` (`:60`) builds a `new Project` (`:64`), and the `const project = options.project ?? createTypeScriptProject(options)` at `:78` is NEVER released - the AST and the compiler stay resident for the whole build. `rag-index/ts-chunker-v2.mjs:51` holds a MODULE-SCOPE `import { Node } from ts-morph` binding as well, and because that same file imports `rag-index/ts-chunker.mjs` at `:43-50`, EVERY build loads the compiler even when it never chunks a TypeScript source. On top of that, `rag-index/build-index.mjs:61-62` calls `collectTypeScriptChunksByFilePath` (`:399-415`), which chunks EVERY ts-source document of the build up front and returns ONE Map that holds every ts-source chunk of the build until the index loop ends (it is read by `chunkDocument` at `:386-396`), so the resident chunk set scales with the TOTAL chunk count of the corpus instead of with the work in flight. THE API FACT THAT BINDS THE FIX: the installed ts-morph 27.0.2 has NO `Project.dispose()` and NO `Project.forget()` - the release surfaces that DO exist are `Project.removeSourceFile(sourceFile)` (which calls `sourceFile.forget()`), the inherited `Node.forget()` (which calls `forgetDescendants()` and then `compilerFactory.removeNodeFromCache(this)`) and `project.getLanguageService().compilerObject.dispose()` (the `ts.LanguageService.dispose()` of the TypeScript compiler host). This is the residual defect that the Step-1 GREEN lane measured (the expected post-`P1-S1-5` drop of about 27 MB realised as only -9,195,520 bytes, `V-OBS-025`), and it is owned by the slice `P1-S3-4`.

**The THIRD bounded-memory defect (the per-entity re-read and the retained SlicedString in the entity-graph stage).** MEASURED BY THE `P1-S3-3` GREEN LANE. `rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs:373-396` (`buildHeadingTextMap`) calls `readFile` on the WHOLE FILE once per DOCUMENT ENTITY and retains `content.slice(char_start, char_end)` for every heading it keeps; a V8 SlicedString PINS ITS ENTIRE PARENT BUFFER, so the resident set scales with (the number of entities x the size of the file) instead of with the text actually kept. `collectDocDocuments()` (`:347`) is derived from the FILESYSTEM and is NOT freshness-gated, so every corpus document is materialised on every run. The measured read amplification is **6,584 file reads totalling 5,239,687,219 bytes for 25,845,342 bytes of entity text - 203x** - dominated by the `.logs.md` trackers (`plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md`, 9,311,682 bytes x 525 entities, about 4.89 GB of retained parent buffers). The consequence is a DETERMINISTIC ABORT: `npm run rag:update` dies at the `build-graph` stage with exit code **134** and `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit` at 8191.7 MB, identically over two runs, with a peak working set of **11,324,051,456 bytes (10.80 GiB)** against the ambient 8,192 MB Node heap cap. The SAME stage exits 0 at `--max-old-space-size=12288` with **10,277 entities / 25,957 edges** (code 3,693 / 20,259, doc 6,584 / 5,595, cross-ref 103), so the defect is the RETENTION and not the output. The SAME defect is why `rag-index/__tests__/build-entity-graph.red.test.mjs` and `rag-index/__tests__/graph-term.turso.test.mjs` crash today with "Jest worker ran out of memory and crashed" - both suites were classified PRE-EXISTING and UNOWNED by the `P1-S1-1` and `P1-S1-2` lanes. This defect is owned by the NEW slice `P1-S3-5` (PLAN AMENDMENT RECORD A7).

**The corpus-identity hole (the family assignment is not part of the identity).** The corpus identity that the incremental updater computes and stores - the digest the idempotent `build-graph` skip compares - is built from `file_path|sha256|mtime_ms|file_size` (`rag-index/update-rag.mjs`, the identity row query and the stored corpus hash): it carries NO `doc_family`, even though the schema has the column (`documents.doc_family TEXT NOT NULL`, `rag-index/schema-turso.sql:22`). SO THE FILTERED PLAN-SHAPED QUERY MATCHES **ZERO** ROWS, THE BROADEN-ON-EMPTY NET FIRES, AND THE RESPONSE COMES BACK WITH ROWS FROM **ANY** FAMILY WHILE REPORTING `family_fallback: true` / `classification_fallback: true`. THE LEAK IS SILENT FROM THE CALLER'S POINT OF VIEW BECAUSE THE FLAGS ARE COLLAPSED INTO ONE BOOLEAN THAT THE CALLER MAY NOT READ.

### THE P2-S4-1 REOPENED EXECUTION RECORD - THE FOCUSED DENSE CSV/FILTER RED CONTRACT (THE `03-red-testing` LANE)

**WHAT THIS LANE DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** IT AUTHORED THE THIRD OWNED FILE - `rag-index/__tests__/query-dense-family-set.red.test.mjs` - A JEST `.mjs` RED HOME THAT DRIVES THE **REAL** `queryDenseIndex` OF `rag-index/query-dense.mjs` OVER A CONTROLLED DB CLIENT AND MEASURES THE THREE SINGLE-FAMILY SQL SITES OF THE DENSE PATH; IT REPAIRED THE MOCK FACTORY OF THE OWNER-LOCAL HOME `rag-index/query-dense.test.mjs` SO THE SEVEN FAMILY LANES OF THAT HOME SURVIVE THE UPCOMING SOURCE CHANGE; IT CONFIRMED THAT THE THREE CSV LANES ARE RED **BY ASSERTION** FOR THE INTENDED REASON (THE ROUTED CSV IS BOUND AS ONE EQUALITY PARAMETER, SO IT MATCHES ZERO DENSE ROWS WHILE THE DENSE INDEX IS WARM); IT TOOK THREE TIER-3 DELEGATIONS THROUGH VALIDATED DISPATCH PACKETS OVER DISJOINT FILE SETS PLUS ONE TIER-3 READ-ONLY `slice-validator` REVIEW; IT RECORDED THE MEASURED TRANSCRIPTS IN THE `red_evidence:` BLOCK AND HERE; AND IT CHANGED **NO** PRODUCTION SOURCE BYTE. **NO MUTATING GIT COMMAND WAS RUN.**

**THE DEFECT THE DENSE RED CONTRACT PINS (THE MEASURED CAUSE, NOT A GUESS).** THE ROUTING PUBLISHES A **CSV** FAMILY LIST - `rag-index/routing-table.mjs:103` -> `ROUTING.plan_specific.family = "plan,completed-plan"` - BUT ALL **THREE** SINGLE-FAMILY SQL SITES OF THE DENSE PATH COMPARE THAT WHOLE CSV FOR **EQUALITY** AGAINST ONE COLUMN: `const familyFilter = family ? 'AND d.doc_family = ?' : '';` AT `rag-index/query-dense.mjs:199` (THE BM25 CANDIDATE LOADER), `:309` (THE ANN CANDIDATE PATH) AND `:372` (THE DENSE TOP-K / BRUTE-FORCE PATH). THE ROUTED CSV IS THEREFORE BOUND AS **ONE** EQUALITY PARAMETER, **NO** DOCUMENT CARRIES THE LITERAL FAMILY NAME `plan,completed-plan`, AND THE ROUTED FILTER MATCHES **ZERO** DENSE ROWS WHILE THE DENSE INDEX IS WARM. THE REUSABLE SET-FILTER HELPER THAT PUBLISHES THE CORRECT SHAPE ALREADY EXISTS - `compileFamilySetFilter` AT `rag-index/metadata-filter.mjs:802` (DELEGATING TO `parseFamilySet` AT `:768`), WHICH EMITS `d.doc_family IN (?, ?)` WITH ONE BOUND PARAMETER PER FAMILY FOR A CSV OF TWO OR MORE MEMBERS, `d.doc_family = ?` WITH EXACTLY ONE BOUND PARAMETER FOR A SINGLE MEMBER, AND NOTHING AT ALL WHEN NO FAMILY IS ROUTED.

**THE FIVE DENSE LANES, THEIR MEASURED VALUES AND THEIR STATE.**

| #   | the lane                                                                                       | the dense SQL site              | MEASURED TODAY                                                                                       | EXPECTED                                                    | STATE   |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| 1   | `binds the routed plan-family set as separate parameters in the BM25 candidate SQL`            | `rag-index/query-dense.mjs:199` | `predicate: "d.doc_family = ?"`, `placeholderCount: 1`, `boundFamilyValues: ["plan,completed-plan"]` | `"d.doc_family IN (?,?)"`, `2`, `["completed-plan","plan"]` | **RED** |
| 2   | `binds the routed plan-family set as separate parameters in the ANN candidate SQL`             | `:309`                          | the same three values                                                                                | the same three values                                       | **RED** |
| 3   | `binds the routed plan-family set as separate parameters in the dense top-k / brute-force SQL` | `:372`                          | the same three values                                                                                | the same three values                                       | **RED** |
| 4   | `carries no document-family predicate when no family is routed`                                | all three                       | `null` at all three sites                                                                            | `null` at all three sites                                   | GREEN   |
| 5   | `keeps the single-family equality predicate with exactly one bound parameter`                  | all three                       | `d.doc_family = ?` / `1` at all three sites                                                          | the same                                                    | GREEN   |

**LANES 4 AND 5 ARE GREEN BY DESIGN AND ARE NOT RED LANES.** LANE 4 EXISTS SO A FIX THAT SIMPLY **DROPPED** THE FAMILY PREDICATE COULD NOT SATISFY LANES 1 TO 3 BY DELETING THE FILTER (A DROPPED PREDICATE MEASURES AS `null` / `0` / `[]`, WHICH IS NOT THE EXPECTED CONTRACT). LANE 5 EXISTS SO THE FIX CANNOT REGRESS THE SINGLE-FAMILY CASE - THE SINGLE-FAMILY SQL MUST KEEP ITS EXACT CURRENT SHAPE (`d.doc_family = ?` WITH EXACTLY ONE BOUND PARAMETER).

**THE EXPECTED CONTRACT IS DERIVED, NOT RE-TYPED - WHICH IS WHY THE RED HOME CANNOT GO VACUOUS.** THE EXPECTED PREDICATE AND THE EXPECTED BOUND VALUES ARE COMPILED **AT TEST TIME BY THE REAL** `compileFamilySetFilter` OF THE REAL `rag-index/metadata-filter.mjs` (WHICH THIS HOME DOES **NOT** `jest.unstable_mockModule`), SO THE HOME MEASURES THE PRODUCTION SQL AGAINST THE REAL HELPER RATHER THAN AGAINST A HAND-WRITTEN STRING. THE FAMILY VALUE ITSELF IS READ FROM THE ROUTING TABLE (`ROUTING.plan_specific.family`) AND IS NEVER RE-TYPED, SO THE HOME FOLLOWS THE ROUTING IF THE ROUTING CHANGES.

**WHAT THIS LANE DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** IT AUTHORED THE ONE FILE THE SLICE OWNS - `rag-index/__tests__/plan-first-ranking.red.test.mjs` - A JEST `.mjs` RED HOME THAT MEASURES THE **REAL** PUBLISHED FAMILY PRIORITY AND THE **REAL** ORDERING SEAM OF `rag-index/assemble-context.mjs` AND SCANS THE **REAL** SOURCE TEXT OF `scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-advanced.mjs`; IT CONFIRMED THAT THE HOME IS RED **BY ASSERTION** FOR THE INTENDED REASON (THE PLAN FAMILIES ARE NOT AT THE HEAD OF THE PUBLISHED PRIORITY, THE ORDERING SEAM PUTS THE SOURCE FAMILY AHEAD OF A PLAN FAMILY AT AN EQUAL SCORE, THE RETIRED `readme` FAMILY IS STILL PUBLISHED IN THE PRIORITY, AND THE ADVANCED-SEARCH MODULE STILL CARRIES THE DEAD GENERATED-README SUPPRESSION); IT TOOK TWO TIER-3 DELEGATIONS THROUGH VALIDATED DISPATCH PACKETS (A TIER-3 `unit-test-writer` THAT AUTHORED THE HOME AND A TIER-3 READ-ONLY `slice-validator` THAT REVIEWED THE CONTRACT); IT AMENDED ITS OWN HOME AGAINST THE REVIEWER MEDIUM FINDING AND RE-MEASURED IT; IT RECORDED THE MEASURED TRANSCRIPTS IN THE `red_evidence:` BLOCK AND HERE; AND IT CHANGED **NO** PRODUCTION, TEST (OTHER THAN ITS OWN RED HOME), SPEC, FIXTURE, INDEX, SQL OR CORPUS BYTE. **NO MUTATING GIT COMMAND WAS RUN.**

**THE DEFECT THE RED CONTRACT PINS (THE MEASURED CAUSE, NOT A GUESS).** TWO SEPARATE FACTS SIT ON TWO SEAMS, AND THE SLICE OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE, SO BOTH SETS OF LANES LIVE IN THE SAME HOME. (1) **THE PRIORITY SEAM.** THE PUBLISHED PRIORITY OF `rag-index/assemble-context.mjs` (`DEFAULT_FAMILY_PRIORITY`, `:53-60`) IS `["ts-source","readme","plan","agent","skill","demo"]` - SO THE SOURCE FAMILY RANKS **FIRST**, THE RETIRED `readme` FAMILY RANKS **SECOND** (AND THE CORPUS CAN NO LONGER PUBLISH IT), THE PLAN FAMILY RANKS **THIRD**, AND THE `completed-plan` FAMILY IS **NOT IN THE LIST AT ALL**. THE ORDINAL HELPER `familyPriorityOrdinal` (`:375-380`) RESOLVES AN ABSENT FAMILY TO `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, SO `completed-plan` SORTS **LAST**, NOT FIRST - AND A RAW `indexOf` WOULD HAVE RETURNED `-1` AND MADE THAT COMPARISON **VACUOUSLY GREEN** TODAY. THE FAMILY DELTA INSIDE `orderChunks` (`:394`) IS A TIE-BREAK AFTER THE TIER DELTA AND THE FILE-MAX DELTA AND IT OUTRANKS THE FILE-PATH FALLBACK, SO AT AN EQUAL SCORE THE **SOURCE** CHUNK SORTS FIRST. (2) **THE SUPPRESSION SEAM.** THE ADVANCED-SEARCH MODULE STILL DECLARES `README_FAMILY = "readme"` (`:84`) AND `GENERATED_README_FAMILY = "generated-readme"` (`:85`) AND FILTERS ON BOTH (`:857-863`, THE COMPARISONS AT `:860-861`) UNDER THE `include_code_only` OPTION - BUT THE CORPUS PUBLISHES NINE FAMILIES (`CORPUS_FAMILY_NAMES`, `rag-index/corpus-sources.mjs:202`) AND NEITHER `readme` NOR `generated-readme` IS AMONG THEM, SO THE SUPPRESSION FILTERS **NOTHING** OUT: IT IS A **DEAD BRANCH** THAT THE CORPUS CHANGE MADE DEAD.

**THE FAMILY NAMES ARE DERIVED, NOT RE-TYPED - WHICH IS WHY THE HOME CANNOT GO VACUOUS.** THE SOURCE FAMILY COMES FROM `ROUTING.code_specific.family` AND THE PLAN FAMILIES FROM `ROUTING.plan_specific.family` (THE CSV `plan,completed-plan`) OF `rag-index/routing-table.mjs`, SO THE HOME FOLLOWS THE ROUTING IF THE ROUTING CHANGES. **THE `AC-406-A` LANES MEASURE THE SUPPRESSION AT THE SOURCE LEVEL, AND THAT IS THE STRONGER PROBE - NOT A WEAKER PROXY.** `scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-advanced.mjs` IS **NEVER IMPORTED** BY THIS HOME: IT IS READ AS TEXT THROUGH `node:fs`, RESOLVED FROM THE HOME URL ITSELF (`fileURLToPath(new URL("../../scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-advanced.mjs", import.meta.url))`). THE REASON IS TWOFOLD. (a) THE `rag-index-mjs` JEST PROJECT HAS **NO** SETUP FILE, WHILE THE `mcp-semantic-mjs` ONE EXISTS PRECISELY TO FORCE THE DENSE AND RERANKER STATES TO `cold` "without loading onnxruntime-node native bindings, which can crash during Jest teardown" - SO IMPORTING THE MODULE INTO THIS PROJECT WOULD CARRY A NATIVE-BINDING RISK THAT THE SLICE FORBIDS. (b) **THE SCAN IS ALSO THE STRONGER MEASUREMENT:** BECAUSE THE CORPUS CAN NO LONGER PUBLISH THE RETIRED FAMILIES, THE SUPPRESSION FILTERS **NOTHING** OUT, SO A BEHAVIOURAL ASSERTION OVER SEARCH RESULTS WOULD BE **VACUOUS** - BYTE-IDENTICAL BEFORE AND AFTER THE FIX - WHILE THE SOURCE-LEVEL SCAN MEASURES THE SUPPRESSION ITSELF. THE COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED BEFORE THE LITERAL SCAN (BLOCK COMMENTS AND LINE COMMENTS, WITH A `//` THAT FOLLOWS A COLON EXCLUDED SO A URL INSIDE A STRING SURVIVES), SO A COMMENT MENTIONING A RETIRED FAMILY CANNOT MASQUERADE AS A LIVE REFERENCE.
